column2: Two years have passed since I swore to take back the south, and not one blow has been struck. The levies have drifted home to their fields, the ship-owners have found better-paying cargo, and the taverns of my capital have started to joke about my oath.\n\nThe moment has passed.
Another time, perhaps.

[Root.GetTitledName]

When you march to take back the south, my banners will march with yours. Send word, and I will come.

Your ally,
[From.GetTitledName]
A true friend of the south.

[Root.GetTitledName]

The hour has come. My host marches against the occupiers, and I hold you to your promise. Bring your swords.

[From.GetTitledName]
I gave my word. We ride.
The Condottiere

Twice now the lords of the south have marched to take these lands back, and twice I have stood against them, faithful to the gods of the Old World and faithful to whoever paid me. The reconquistadors call me a traitor. The occupiers call me a heathen. Both of them pay me.\n\nIn the taverns from Magritta to Miragliano they sing of me as the finest captain of the age, and they are not wrong. My children will inherit my sword, my name and my price.
Loyalty is expensive. Skill more so.
The Reconqueror

Land by land, I have torn the south back from the hands of those who took it. Where foreign banners flew there are temples of the Old World gods again, and the people line the roads to throw flowers under the hooves of my horse.\n\nThe priests already call me the Reconqueror, and an old helm that is said to have belonged to one of the captains who drove Jaffar's host into the sea was brought out of a temple vault for me. My line will be remembered as long as the south is free.
The south is ours again.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I hear you are at war, and that the war is not going as well as it could. I have men, I have horses, and I am not overly troubled about whose side the gods are on. For a fair price my swords are yours.

[FromFrom.GetTitledName]
Name your price.
I do not hire turncoats.

[Root.GetTitledName]

Your terms are accepted. The gold is on its way. See that your swords earn it.

[From.GetTitledName]
Excellent.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I would rather lose this war than win it with the help of a sellsword who has no loyalty but to his purse. Keep your swords.

[From.GetTitledName]
Their loss.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I am at war over the south, and I am told your swords can be bought. I will pay well if you fight for me, and I will not ask what your priests think of it.

[FromFrom.GetTitledName]
Gold is gold. I will fight.
Some things are not for sale.

[Root.GetTitledName]

The gold is received. My swords march to join yours.

[From.GetTitledName]
Good.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I am not a sellsword, whatever you may have heard. Find someone else to bleed for you.

[From.GetTitledName]
Pity.

My marshal brings the muster rolls. Every village in the realm can give men for the war, but men without arms, training or pay are little better than a mob.\n\n"How much are we willing to spend, my [Root.GetLordLady]?"
Give them spears and bows.
Arm them properly.
Only the best: pikes, horses, armour.
Not a single crown. Let them bring their pitchforks.

A messenger arrives from [Root.RelHead.GetTitledName]. The temple has heard of my oath to take back the south, and its coffers are open to me, for a price. The priests will want a share of the glory, and a share of my devotion, in return.\n\nOr I could tell them that this war is between me and the gods, and needs no priest's gold.
I will take a little of the temple's gold.
I will take all the temple can give.
The gods' blessing is enough.

A scarred captain presents [new_commander.GetHerselfHimself] at court. [new_commander.GetFirstName] has fought Arabyans in the dunes, greenskins in the Border Princes and pirates off Sartosa, and has heard that I am raising a host to take back the south.\n\n"I have led men into worse places than the ones you are going, my [Root.GetLordLady]. Give me a command and I will show you."
Stay at my court.
Take a command.
I have captains enough.

The land of the occupiers lies across the water as often as over the hills, and an army without ships will march a long way round. The ship-owners of my ports, and a Tilean merchant prince or two, offer to hire out their galleys for the war, at a price.
Hire the galleys.
We will march.

The year of preparation is over. The levies are drilled, the captains chosen, the galleys waiting in harbour. Everyone in the realm knows what comes next.\n\nThe south will be free again, or I will die trying.
To war!
An Oath for the South

[From.GetTitledName] has sworn before the altars of [From.Religion.GetName] to take back the lands of Estalia and Tilea that are held by foreign masters. Long ago the Sultan Jaffar's host landed in Estalia and was flung back into the sea, and [From.GetTitledName] means to do it again, to the Sultans and to every other invader who has taken a foothold in the south.\n\nThe levies are already mustering. In a year, perhaps two, the host will march.
May the gods guide [From.GetHerHis] sword.
Let them come. We will be waiting.
The South Is Free

The last foreign banner in Estalia and Tilea has been torn down. From the Irrana Mountains to the Tilean Sea, every land of the south is held by lords who bow to the gods of the Old World.\n\nThe temples ring their bells, the merchants count the trade that will flow again, and old soldiers tell the young ones about the war. The Reconquest of the South is over.
Praise the gods!
They have won, for now.

A young [From.GetWomanMan] with a fine sword and a finer tongue has come to court. [From.GetSheHeCap] is [From.GetFirstName], an adventurer of [From.Culture.GetName] blood who has sworn to win back the lands of the south from their foreign masters, with or without the help of [From.GetHerHis] betters.\n\n"I ask only your blessing, my [Root.GetLordLady], and whatever else you see fit to give. The men will follow me. The gods will do the rest."
You have my blessing, and more.
I want no part of this.
[FromFrom.GetFirstName] is preparing to march, and my court is waiting to see what kind of patron I will be. My name, my prayers or my purse: any of them would help the young adventurer's cause.
Let [FromFrom.GetHerHim] fight under my banner.
I will pray for [FromFrom.GetHerHis] victory.
Take some gold.
My blessing is enough.
Swear the Reconquest
Swear to take back the lands of Estalia and Tilea from their foreign masters: a year of preparation, then war, land by land. An oath like this is sworn once in a lifetime.
Promise to Join the Reconquest
Promise to join §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! when [Root.GetSheHe] marches to take back the south.
Sell Your Sword to the Occupiers
Offer your swords to §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! against the Reconquest, for gold.
Hire a Faithful Sellsword
Offer §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! gold to fight for you against the Reconquest.
Sell Your Sword to the Reconquest
Offer your swords to §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! for the Reconquest, for gold.
Hire a Foreign Sellsword
Offer §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! gold to fight for the Reconquest.
No other Reconquest of the South is under way
The Reconquest is still led by the one who swore it
The Reconquest
Condottiere Blood of [Root.GetFirstName]
A faithful captain who twice threw back the Reconquest of the South for foreign gold, remembered as the finest sellsword of [Root.GetHerHis] age.
Reconqueror Blood of [Root.GetFirstName]
The lord who tore the lands of the south back from their foreign masters.
Reconqueror's Helm
An old helm said to have been worn by one of the captains who threw the Sultan Jaffar's host back into the sea.
Can §YSwear the Reconquest§! §Gmore cheaply§!
§BHoly Fury:§! Reconquest of the South
Estalian and Tilean lords may swear to take back the south, and adventurers may do it for them.
Estalian and Tilean lords may swear to take back the south, but adventurers do not appear.
There is no Reconquest of the South.
